newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares rebound strongly, close 1.03pct highe.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares rebound strongly, close 1.03pct highe.

text.p: Greek shares gained momentum after chalking up mild gains early in the session and closed 1.03 percent higher in a broad advance in moderate turnover. Brokers said the market was bound to test 945 points on the upside soon.
Construction and industrials led the advance with banks and small-caps also trading stronger.

"We had a good market today, it was a good reaction to the upside helped by some short-covering. I think we have more to go, stocks are undervalued and will test the 945 resistance area. If this level is overcome then we're headed towards 980 points," said investment advisor Iakovos Diamantopoulos at Hermes Brokerage.
Construction shares rebounded convincingly today and although volatile they promise higher returns until year end, he said.

Friday's upside reaction came amid expectations that the government is planning to tax interest earned on T-bills, derivatives such as swaps, options and FRAs and revamp the tax status of mutual funds as the market awaits the 1997 budget.
The finance ministry cut 40 basis point cut in the marker 12-month T-bill, down to 12.30 percent. The issue came to market on Thursday and sold very well.
National Bank of Greece said on Friday it will trim its savings deposit rate by 25 basis points down to 11.25 percent effective November 4.

"There is good news out there but the market was not reacting. A stable economic policy, a likely tax on interest income earned on state debt paper, I think we're bound to see a pent up reaction by the equities market soon," said Diamantopoulos.
